question: Name the first Indian newspaper that became available on the Internet.
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Hindu**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Hindu was the first Indian newspaper to be available online,** launching its online edition in 1995. 
 
• It launched its online edition on **November 1, 1995**, making it the pioneer among Indian newspapers in the digital space.
 
• The online edition provided key articles from the printed newspaper, enabling readers from across the world to access Indian news and opinions in real time.
 
• The **Kasturi & Sons Limited, the publishers of *The Hindu*, anticipated the growing influence of the Internet and took an early lead in digital** transformation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bengal Gazette

 
 
• The **first newspaper to be published in India was Hicky's Bengal Gazette, which was released on January 29, 1780.** 
 
• Bengal Gazette was the first English-language newspaper published on the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It was founded in Calcutta, by Irishman James Augustus Hicky in 1779.
 
• The newspaper was a strong critic of the administration of Governor-General Warren Hastings.
 
• The newspaper was important for its provocative journalism and its fight for free expression in India
 
• The first newspaper to be published online was The Columbus Dispatch, which went online on July 1, 1980
 
 
 
• The Times of India
 
 
• ​The Times of India issued its first edition on 3 November 1838 as The Bombay Times and Journal of Commerce.
 
• The paper was published on Wednesdays and Saturdays under the direction of Raobahadur Narayan Dinanath Velkar, a Maharashtrian social reformer.
 
• J. E. Brennan was its first editor.
 
• It is the third-largest newspaper in India by circulation and the largest selling English-language daily in the world.
